content.user_title: Research Topics Across Web, Docs, and Code
content.value_statement: Research questions can become slow and inconsistent when sources are checked separately. This skill coordinates parallel searches and produces sourced findings with explicit confidence labels.
actual_capabilities: Selects quick, standard, or extensive research based on required depth and response time.
Coordinates parallel researchers across web sources, local documentation, and code.
Assigns varied search angles for broader coverage in extensive mode.
Cross-validates findings across source types and identifies conflicting information.
Produces structured reports with citations, implementation notes, recommendations, and confidence labels.
Returns available findings and marks incomplete sources when researchers time out.
limitations: Web research requires network access and cannot retrieve paywalled content.
Quick mode uses limited cross-validation and does not search code examples.
Extensive mode requires more agent calls, time, and model capacity.
Confidence labels reflect source agreement and do not guarantee factual accuracy.

use_cases.title: Investigate an API Implementation
use_cases.description: Find current guidance, local documentation, and existing code patterns before implementing an API integration.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sourced Technical Guidance
use_cases.description: Collect verified material, citations, and conflicting viewpoints for a technical guide or internal reference.

use_cases.title: Compare Architecture Options
use_cases.description: Evaluate technologies across official guidance, community experience, local constraints, implementation evidence, and cost.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quick mode to verify [claim]. Check one current web source and local documentation, then give a concise answer, citations, and confidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a fast fact check.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Technical Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Use standard mode to research [technical question]. Search web, local documentation, and code examples in parallel. Cross-check findings and include implementation notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs balanced implementation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use extensive mode to compare [option A] and [option B] for [context]. Cover official guidance, community perspectives, local code, conflicts, costs, and recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a detailed technology comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Architecture Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Use extensive mode to evaluate [architecture decision] under [constraints]. Assign distinct research angles, verify claims across source types, explain disagreements, and identify remaining evidence gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A technical leader needs evidence for a high-impact decision.

output_examples.input: Verify whether quick mode searches code examples.
output_examples.output: Answer: Quick mode searches one web source and local documentation. It does not include a code researcher. Source: cookbook/quick-mode.md. Confidence: High.

output_examples.input: Compare two authentication libraries for a latency-sensitive service.
output: Executive summary: Option A fits the stated latency requirement, while Option B offers stronger integration support.
Key findings: Official documentation supports both options. Local code contains examples only for Option A.
Conflicts: Community sources disagree about maintenance effort.
Recommendation: Validate the unsupported integration before deciding. Confidence: Medium.

best_practices: State the research scope, freshness requirements, and acceptable source types before selecting a mode.
Use the least resource-intensive mode that provides enough depth for the decision.
Verify low-confidence and conflicting findings before using them in important decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not use extensive mode for a simple definition or isolated fact.
Do not place secrets, private data, or confidential code in web search queries.
Do not treat source agreement as proof or remove citations from the final report.

faq.question: Which sources can this skill research?
faq.answer: It can search current web content, local documentation, project specifications, source code, tests, and configuration examples.

faq.question: How do the three research modes differ?
faq.answer: Quick mode favors speed, standard mode balances coverage, and extensive mode uses more researchers for deeper analysis.

faq.question: Does web research require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. Web searches require connectivity and may be limited by rate limits or paywalls.

faq.question: Does the skill modify source code?
faq.answer: No. Its documented code workflow searches and reads existing files for implementation examples.

faq.question: How are confidence labels assigned?
faq.answer: The skill labels findings by source agreement: high for three sources, medium for two, and low for one.

faq.question: What happens when a researcher times out?
faq.answer: The skill synthesizes available results, identifies pending or incomplete sources, and returns the partial report.
